title: branches.py skeleton: importable CLI, JSON contract, load_format
riskReason: The new CLI runs git and reads the repo config, so a wrong contract misleads every later consumer.

seeds.title: validate_format accepts a leading dash and control or bidi characters
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts a format that starts with '-'. It also accepts control and bidi characters. No caller gives the format to git in this slice. S-002 adds git check-ref-format --branch inside validate_format, and that check rejects these values. Keep the check inside validate_format. Give every later git argument after '--' or as a full ref name.

seeds.title: GIT_MODES_PATH uses abspath, while the scripts use realpath
seeds.detail: GIT_MODES_PATH uses os.path.abspath(__file__). The three scripts use os.path.realpath for their sys.path entry. A symlinked branches.py reads the git-modes.json beside the symlink, not the real file. Use os.path.realpath here too, so one rule applies.

seeds.title: Two tests build the same skill copy
seeds.detail: The new test and 'a git-modes.json that cannot be read' in skills/sdlc/test/branches.test.mjs each copy branches.py into a scratch directory with their own code. Merge the directory and mode-000 shapes into the new shape table, or share one skillCopy helper.

seeds.title: Round-1 architecture findings still open
seeds.detail: load_git_modes has three copies (branches.py, next-action.py, state-write.py). GIT_MODES_PATH in branches.py uses abspath, but the sys.path lines use realpath. Build GIT_MODES_PATH from one realpath SKILL_DIR. The npm test glob does not reach test/testkit/*.test.mjs; widen it or import the testkit self-tests from a top-level test file.

seeds.title: No committed test pins the RecursionError catch in load_git_modes
seeds.detail: Fix round 1 added RecursionError to the except in load_git_modes (branches.py:56). The committed deep-nesting test (branches.test.mjs:257) covers config.json only. Verifier test TC-cli-21 (.sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r1/tests/cli-0/branches.verify-cli.test.mjs) covers a deeply nested git-modes.json, an empty-string mode, a null top level and a dangling symlink. The skill ships git-modes.json, so a hostile shape there is unlikely. Fix: when a later slice touches preflight, add the deep-nesting and empty-string-mode shapes to the test at branches.test.mjs:217.

seeds.title: argparse prefix abbreviation accepted
seeds.detail: allow_abbrev is on, so `parse --rep DIR` is accepted as --repo. The spec names no prefix forms of the flags.

seeds.title: Unicode digits accepted as integers
seeds.detail: type=int accepts non-ASCII digits: `--n '١'` gives n = 1. Later tails could embed a value the user did not type in ASCII.

seeds.title: Repeated flag silently takes the last value
seeds.detail: `parse --branch x --branch y` uses y and does not report bad input.

seeds.title: --help prints usage text, not JSON
seeds.detail: `branches.py parse --help` prints argparse usage text and exits 0. This breaks the one-JSON-object stdout contract for that one invocation.

seeds.title: Non-UTF-8 argv passes through as surrogate escapes
seeds.detail: `--branch $'x\xff'` is echoed as x\udcff. The later parse and name logic should decide whether this is bad input.

seeds.title: argparse accepts flag prefixes
seeds.detail: allow_abbrev is on: parse accepts --r, --re, --rep for --repo and --f to --forma for --format, exit 0 (TC-cli-7). The spec names full flags only. Set allow_abbrev=False on the parser and each subparser.

seeds.title: --n, --round and --part accept negative, huge, padded, underscore and non-ASCII digit values
seeds.detail: type=int accepts -1, 99999999999999999999, ' 3', Arabic-Indic 3, '0003', '1_000' and '+4' (TC-cli-10). Tails in spec §1 need non-negative ASCII integers. The slices that build name() should reject these.

seeds.title: A flag given twice keeps the last value silently
seeds.detail: parse --branch a --branch b exits 0 with branch b (TC-cli-6).

seeds.title: --help prints argparse usage and exits 0, not JSON
seeds.detail: --help, -h and '<command> --help' print usage text on stdout with exit 0 (TC-cli-8). A caller that parses stdout as JSON breaks on it.

seeds.title: A config.json with a UTF-8 BOM is refused
seeds.detail: load_format reads with utf-8, so a BOM gives 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM' and exit 2 (TC-cli-19). Reading with utf-8-sig would accept it.

seeds.title: testkit: copySkill cannot turn an existing file into a directory
seeds.detail: copySkill({files: {'git-modes.json': null}}) throws EEXIST because writeFiles calls mkdirSync on the existing file. Callers must also put the path in omit.

seeds.title: branches.py --help and -h exit through SystemExit in main()
seeds.detail: main(['--help']) and main(['parse','-h']) print argparse usage text on stdout and raise SystemExit(0). An in-process caller gets an exception, not a return code, and the CLI prints usage text, not one JSON object. The spec does not define --help.

seeds.title: A UTF-8 BOM in .sdlc/config.json makes every command without --format exit 2
seeds.detail: load_format opens config.json with encoding utf-8, so a BOM gives 'Unexpected UTF-8 BOM'. Use utf-8-sig to accept it. The spec does not name this case.

seeds.title: A valid --format hides a malformed config.json
seeds.detail: With --format given, load_format is not called, so a command exits 0 while config.json is invalid JSON. Later slices that read other config keys may need to read the config anyway.

seeds.title: A decoy branches.py beside a symlink to a script shadows the real module
seeds.detail: The scripts insert os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) into sys.path. abspath does not resolve symlinks. When janitor.py runs through a symlink in a directory that also holds branches.py, that file is imported (manual probe: decoy exit 97). os.path.realpath closes this. The spec names no symlink case.

seeds.title: branches.py: a decoy branches.py beside a symlinked script wins the import
seeds.detail: The three scripts insert os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) into sys.path. abspath does not resolve symlinks. When a script runs through a symlink, a branches.py beside the symlink is imported in place of the real module (decoy exit 97 for all three scripts). os.path.realpath fixes this. The spec does not define the script directory for a symlink.

seeds.title: branches.py: main(["-h"]) raises SystemExit instead of returning
seeds.detail: main(["-h"]) and main(["parse","--help"]) print argparse usage text and raise SystemExit(0). The spec does not define -h. An importing caller gets an exception, and stdout is not a JSON object.

seeds.title: branches.py: load_format drops a non-string branchFormat, but spec section 4 uses config.get("branchFormat") or default
seeds.detail: load_format returns sdlc/{name} for a truthy non-string branchFormat such as 5. Spec section 4 describes next-action semantics as config.get("branchFormat") or "sdlc/{name}", which keeps 5. The two readings diverge when later slices thread fmt through next-action.py.

seeds.title: branches.py: validate_format accepts NUL and control characters in S-001
seeds.detail: validate_format("sdlc/{name}\x00") and validate_format("a\x01/{name}") return the input. ADR-20261009-024036 assigns git check-ref-format to S-002 (R-017). S-002 must refuse these.

seeds.title: branches.py: a valid --format succeeds although the config is malformed
seeds.detail: parse --format sdlc/{name} exits 0 when .sdlc/config.json holds truncated JSON, because the flag skips load_format. The plan asked only to record this. Preflight can report a malformed config even when the flag is given.

seeds.title: argparse accepts flag prefixes
seeds.detail: build_parser keeps allow_abbrev=True. --rep, --r, --form and --f are accepted as --repo and --format. A later flag with a shared prefix changes their meaning. Set allow_abbrev=False on the parser and the subparsers.

seeds.title: A duplicate flag keeps its last value silently
seeds.detail: --repo /nonexistent --repo R exits 0. --format bad --format sdlc/{name} also exits 0. An appended flag overrides an earlier one without notice.

seeds.title: --n, --round and --part accept unicode digits, padding, underscores and negatives
seeds.detail: type=int accepts Arabic-Indic and fullwidth digits, ' 3', '1_000', '-1' and up to 4300 digits. Later slices put these values in branch names. Use a strict ^[0-9]+$ check when name lands.

seeds.title: Refusal errors echo the whole hostile value
seeds.detail: A 100000-digit --n gives a 100035-char error. A 200000-char --format gives an error of the same size. Clip the echoed value. This is for verify-limits, because the spec states no size limit.

seeds.title: -h and --help print argparse usage on stdout
seeds.detail: Help exits 0 with plain text, not one JSON object. The spec does not define help. A caller that parses stdout as JSON breaks on it.

seeds.title: load_git_modes lets OSError and RecursionError escape
seeds.detail: Make git-modes.json a directory, an unreadable file or a 200000-deep nesting. preflight then exits 1 with a traceback (IsADirectoryError, PermissionError or RecursionError). Catch OSError and RecursionError and raise Fail.

seeds.title: load_format lets RecursionError escape and blocks on a FIFO
seeds.detail: A config.json nested 200000 deep makes every command exit 1 with RecursionError. A FIFO at .sdlc/config.json blocks the command until it is killed. This is for verify-contract (VS-6) and verify-limits.

seeds.title: Invisible and confusable characters pass the format checks
seeds.detail: ZWSP, U+202E and Cyrillic letters pass validate_format. git check-ref-format also accepts them, so S-002 does not refuse them either. Such formats give branch names that read differently from their bytes. The spec does not forbid them.

seeds.title: Scripts now need branches.py beside them
seeds.detail: janitor.py, next-action.py and state-write.py import branches from their own directory. A copy of one script without branches.py fails at import. The slice updates git-modes.test.mjs for this. No other repo code copies the scripts alone.

seeds.title: branches.py resolves git-modes.json with abspath, not realpath
seeds.detail: GIT_MODES_PATH uses os.path.abspath(__file__). When branches.py runs through a symlink, preflight reads git-modes.json beside the symlink and exits 2 with 'is missing'. The three scripts now use realpath. The spec does not require a symlinked run of branches.py.

seeds.title: A --repo directory that cannot be read passes when --format is given
seeds.detail: With mode 000 on --repo, parse exits 2 without --format because the config.json read fails. It exits 0 with --format because _repo checks only os.path.isdir (TC-cli-23). Consider an os.access read check in _repo.

seeds.title: GIT_MODES_PATH still uses abspath, not realpath
seeds.detail: The fix made the three scripts resolve their directory through realpath. branches.py builds GIT_MODES_PATH from os.path.abspath(__file__). A branches.py run through a symlink in another directory reads git-modes.json beside the symlink. This seed is not tested here.

seeds.title: branches.py: load_format reports a NUL in the repo path as invalid JSON
seeds.detail: An in-process caller that passes a repo path with a NUL gets Fail with '<path> is not valid JSON: ValueError: embedded null byte'. The file is never read, so the message names the wrong cause. The CLI cannot receive a NUL in argv.

seeds.title: branches.py: a config.json with an integer over 4300 digits is refused
seeds.detail: Valid JSON with a 5000-digit integer in any key makes load_format raise Fail because of the Python int digits limit, although branchFormat is valid. This is an unlikely config.

seeds.title: An in-process caller with a cached branches module binds it, not the skill's module
seeds.detail: When a process already holds sys.modules['branches'], a script loaded through importlib binds that cached module and ignores the sys.path line (A-31). A test harness that imports another branches.py and then loads next-action.py in the same process tests the wrong module. Repo callers load each script in a new process today, so nothing breaks. Keep that rule for later probes.

seeds.title: branches.py resolves git-modes.json through abspath, not realpath
seeds.detail: GIT_MODES_PATH uses os.path.abspath(__file__). When branches.py runs through a symlink, preflight reads git-modes.json beside the symlink and exits 2 with 'is missing'. The three scripts use realpath. The spec does not require a symlinked run of branches.py.

title: validate_format, split and name
riskReason: validate_format calls git check-ref-format; a wrong pass admits formats whose names the forge rejects.

seeds.title: Branch formats with shell characters pass validation
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts 'sdlc/{name}$(id)' and 'sdlc/{name};rm' because git allows these characters. I ran both. The spec delegates validity to git and the forge, so this is not a defect in S-002. Later slices that put a branch name into a shell string must quote it, or use an argument list.

seeds.title: name() does not check the tail
seeds.detail: An id such as '../x' gives 'sdlc/../x'. Today only validate_format and the tests call name, with a fixed id. Slices that feed ledger ids or CLI input into name (S-004 and later) must check the result before git or a path uses it.

seeds.title: Invisible characters pass validation
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts U+200B because git allows it. I ran 'sdlc/​{name}' and it passed. Such a format gives names that look the same as other names. The spec gives this job to git and the forge rules, so this note is for information only.

seeds.title: KINDS and TAILS list the branch kinds twice
seeds.detail: KINDS and TAILS both list the branch kinds. _kind accepts a kind that tail refuses until S-004 to S-006 add all rows. Fix: when the table is complete, derive KINDS from TAILS, or assert in a test that the two sets are equal.

seeds.title: TAILS constant sits between functions
seeds.detail: TAILS sits between validate_format and tail. The module keeps its other constants at the top. Fix: move TAILS next to KINDS and PLACEHOLDERS.

seeds.title: T-012 name promises a whitespace case it does not test
seeds.detail: The case sdlc/{ name } holds no placeholder, so it fails at the placeholder count, not at the whitespace check. T-018 now pins the whitespace check, so only the name is wrong. Fix: replace the case with 'sdlc/ {name}', or rename the test to say it covers a malformed placeholder.

seeds.title: T-018 tab case does not match the test name
seeds.detail: Git refuses 'sdlc/\tS-001' (exit 128), but the test name says 'Unicode whitespace that git accepts'. Git accepts U+00A0, U+3000 and U+2028. Fix: drop the tab case, or rename the test to 'rejects Unicode and control whitespace'.

seeds.title: Whitespace branch of validate_format has no direct Python test
seeds.detail: sdlc/{ name } fails at the placeholder count, not at the whitespace check. The whitespace branch is reached only by the S-001 CLI case 'sdlc/ {name}'. Add a direct Python case such as 'sdlc /{name}' to pin it.

seeds.title: tail accepts extra parts silently
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id='S-1', extra=1) returns 'S-1' and does not raise Fail. The spec does not say whether extra parts are an error.

seeds.title: A git binary on PATH decides the format verdict
seeds.detail: validate_format runs the first git on PATH. A fake git that exits 0 admits sdlc/{name}.. (TC-cli-11). The spec does not pin the git binary.

seeds.title: Zero-width characters pass validate_format
seeds.detail: U+200B, U+200D and U+FEFF do not match Python \s, and git accepts them, so a​b/{name} is valid (TC-cli-5). The branch names then look the same as names without these characters.

seeds.title: Control characters U+001C to U+001F are reported as whitespace
seeds.detail: Python \s matches U+001C to U+001F, so a\x1f/{name} fails with 'holds whitespace', not with the git reason. The verdict is correct, but the message names the wrong cause.

seeds.title: testkit: cli-runner has no per-run absolute python option
seeds.detail: A test that isolates PATH must build a second runner with cliRunner({ python: <abs path> }), because python3 is found through the child PATH.

seeds.title: Zero-width and BOM characters pass validate_format
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts formats with U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF and U+180E. These characters are not Unicode whitespace, and git accepts them, so a branch name can hold an invisible character. The spec forbids only whitespace. Consider refusing Unicode format characters (category Cf).

seeds.title: The first git on PATH decides the validate_format verdict
seeds.detail: A fake git on PATH that exits 0 makes validate_format accept sdlc/{name}... The spec does not define which git runs. Consider naming the git binary in the pre-flight output.

seeds.title: Control characters U+001C to U+001F fail as whitespace
seeds.detail: Python re \s matches U+001C to U+001F. validate_format therefore refuses a\x1f/{name} with the message 'holds whitespace', not with the git control-character reason. The verdict is correct. Only the message text is misleading.

seeds.title: name accepts a non-string id and stringifies it
seeds.detail: name("sdlc/{name}", "slice", id=False) gives sdlc/False, id=[] gives sdlc/[] and id={} gives sdlc/{}. tail checks only None and the empty string. A Fail for an id that is not a str keeps such names out of git.

seeds.title: name does not check the id text against git
seeds.detail: name gives sdlc/.., 'sdlc/ ' and sdlc/S-001.lock without Fail. validate_format checks only the sample id S-001. A caller that passes an operator id gets a name that git check-ref-format refuses later.

seeds.title: an unhashable kind raises TypeError, not Fail
seeds.detail: tail uses TAILS.get(kind), so a list or a dict kind raises TypeError. Every other unknown kind raises Fail. An isinstance check on kind makes the Fail contract total.

seeds.title: testkit: pycall cannot pass keyword arguments
seeds.detail: callPython calls fn(*args) only. name and tail take **parts, so the verifier wrote a shim module with name_kw(fmt, kind, parts). A kwargs field in the pycall request removes the shim.

seeds.title: Invisible and terminal-control characters pass the format check
seeds.detail: validate_format accepts U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+FEFF, U+2060, U+180E and C1 U+009B (CSI) in the literal part, because git accepts them. A branch name can then look the same as another name or carry a terminal escape. The spec delegates this check to git, so it is not a defect.

seeds.title: Formats that start with refs/heads/, HEAD or @ pass
seeds.detail: refs/heads/{name}, refs/{name}, HEAD{name} and @{name} pass git check-ref-format --branch. refs/heads/{name} gives the branch refs/heads/refs/heads/S-001, which is ambiguous with refs.

seeds.title: A lone surrogate in a Python-side format passes
seeds.detail: validate_format('a\udc80/{name}') returns the format. Python passes byte 0x80 to git, and git accepts it. The format is not valid Unicode, so later JSON or forge calls can treat it differently.

seeds.title: S-001 TC-* evidence tests are missing
seeds.detail: The evidence.tests of R-014, R-016 and R-098 list TC-* tests under .sdlc/slices/S-001/verification/r1/tests/. Those files exist in neither the branch nor the main tree, so no lens can run them again.

seeds.title: T-012 whitespace case reaches the placeholder check, not the whitespace check
seeds.detail: The T-012 case sdlc/{ name } raises Fail at the placeholder count (found 0). T-018 now covers the whitespace branch, so only the T-012 case name is misleading.

seeds.title: tail accepts extra parts
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id='S-1', extra=1) returns S-1 and raises no Fail. The spec does not say whether extra parts are an error.

title: tail contract and format resolution order
riskReason: The resolution order decides which format every branch gets; a wrong order silently renames future branches.

seeds.title: name does not check the parts it puts in the branch name
seeds.detail: Carried from round 0. `name --kind slice --id=-c --format '{name}'` prints the branch `-c` with exit 0, and git can read it as an option. `name --kind e2e-area --id M-1 --area '../x y'` prints `sdlc/M-1-e2e-../x y` with exit 0. validate_format checks only the S-001 sample. The spec does not ask for a part check, and the parts come from ledger ids, so this is hardening. Fix: in cmd_name, run the built branch through `git check-ref-format --branch`. Consumers must put `--` before a branch name in git commands.

seeds.title: cmd_preflight reads config twice; given depends on operand order
seeds.detail: _format reads config.json through load_format, and given reads it again through _config_format. Swapping the operands of the given expression makes preflight with --format fail on a broken config. T-024 now guards this. Fix: read _config_format(repo) one time only when --format is absent, and derive fmt and given from that one value.

seeds.title: NAME_PARTS repeats the name sub-parser part flags
seeds.detail: A new part flag must change two places. Fix: build the name sub-parser part flags from NAME_PARTS, or keep the two side by side.

seeds.title: brokenConfigRepos overlaps existing broken-config fixtures
seeds.detail: The new fixture builds invalid JSON and deep-nesting configs that the deep-nesting test and withConfig also build. Fix: when a later slice needs broken configs, reuse brokenConfigRepos instead of a new fixture.

seeds.title: T-024 does not restore the mode of the unreadable config
seeds.detail: The git-modes test restores the file mode to 0o644 in a finally block. T-024 leaves config.json at mode 000. Scratch cleanup still removes it, so nothing fails now, but the two tests are not consistent. Restore the mode in a finally block.

seeds.title: T-019 still has no case for an empty ts
seeds.detail: Round 0 reported this gap. The plan says the state tail treats an empty ts as absent. Add tail("state", ts="") to T-019 and assert ^state-\d{14}$.

seeds.title: Fail message article
seeds.detail: tail's Fail message reads 'a e2e-area branch name needs a non-empty ...'. The article before a vowel is wrong. The spec does not define this text.

seeds.title: branches.py --help prints argparse text, not JSON
seeds.detail: branches.py name --help prints the argparse usage text and exits 0. The spec does not define --help, so this is not a defect. A caller that parses stdout as JSON gets text here.

seeds.title: preflight output still echoes an interim args object
seeds.detail: preflight prints {ok, command, format, args, given}. The args echo holds the absolute repo path. A later slice that defines the preflight output must decide whether args stays.

seeds.title: The missing-part error says 'a e2e-area branch name'
seeds.detail: The message puts the article 'a' before every kind. The meaning is correct, but the text reads badly for e2e-area.

seeds.title: name gives a branch that git refuses for a part with git-unsafe characters
seeds.detail: validate_format checks only the format, with the sample id S-001. name does not run git check-ref-format on the full name. The ids ../x, 'a b', x..y, x~1, a:b, x.lock, * and @{1} give branches that git refuses, and name still exits 0. The spec validates only the format. A later slice that creates branches from these names must check them. Transcripts: .sdlc/slices/S-003/verification/r0/logs/cli-1-seeds.txt.

seeds.title: the integer flags take unicode digits, padded values and underscores
seeds.detail: argparse type=int uses Python int(). So --n=٣, --n=１２, --n=' 3 ', --n=1_000, --n=+1 and --n=9223372036854775808 all exit 0. No S-003 row consumes these parts. When the verify and attempt rows land in S-004 to S-006, --n=٣ and --n=3 will give the same branch. Decide whether that is the intended result. List: .sdlc/slices/S-003/verification/r0/logs/cli-1-TC-cli-105-accepted.txt.

seeds.title: name --help prints plain help text and exits 0, not one JSON object
seeds.detail: branches.py name --help prints the argparse usage text and exits 0. Every other path prints one JSON object. The spec does not define --help. A caller that parses stdout as JSON fails on this output. A flag-like part value never reaches this path (TC-cli-104).

seeds.title: branches.py exposes helpers the spec does not name
seeds.detail: cmd_name, cmd_parse, cmd_list, cmd_preflight, build_parser, JsonArgumentParser, NAME_PARTS, TAILS and the imported datetime and timezone are public names. The spec API names only load_format, validate_format, tail, name, split, parse, list_kind, read_rules, evaluate and derive. Prefix the helpers with an underscore, or declare __all__.

seeds.title: load_format accepts the non-standard JSON values NaN and Infinity
seeds.detail: A config.json whose text is NaN or Infinity, or {"branchFormat": NaN}, gives the default and not a Fail. A config file with a UTF-8 BOM gives a Fail. No requirement covers these shapes.

seeds.title: testkit: callPython has no keyword arguments and no TZ control
seeds.detail: callPython passes positional arguments only and fixes the environment. tail and name take keyword parts, and the state check needs TZ. The contract tests use a small local consumer helper. Add kwargs and env options to callPython.

seeds.title: tail accepts a non-string part and a non-digit ts
seeds.detail: tail('slice', id=0) returns '0', and tail('state', ts='abc') returns 'state-abc'. The later parse() reads state tails with ^state-(\d{14})$, so it does not classify a branch made from a non-digit ts.

seeds.title: name gives git-invalid branch names for hostile parts
seeds.detail: name does not run git check-ref-format on the full name. --id '../..', 'a b', 'HEAD@{1}', '*' or a tab give exit 0 with branches that git check-ref-format --branch refuses. The spec validates only the format.

seeds.title: integer flags accept unicode digits, padding and underscores
seeds.detail: argparse type=int uses Python int(), so '٣', '１２', ' 3 ', NBSP-padded 3 and '1_000' are accepted. When n, round or part reach a branch name in S-004 to S-006, the name can differ from the operator's text.

seeds.title: invalid UTF-8 in a part gives lone surrogate escapes in the JSON output
seeds.detail: Raw bytes \xff\xfe in --id give branch 'sdlc/\udcff\udcfe' with exit 0. Strict JSON readers can refuse or replace lone surrogates.

seeds.title: argparse error echoes an oversized value in full
seeds.detail: --round with 100000 digits gives one JSON error that holds all the digits. The spec states no limit, so this seed goes to verify-limits.

seeds.title: testkit: cli-runner cannot pass raw bytes in argv
seeds.detail: Node spawn takes only strings, so a test with invalid UTF-8 argv needs a Python relay. A run option for byte arguments would remove that relay.

seeds.title: Done-requirement evidence points at pruned verification tests
seeds.detail: requirements.json evidence.tests for R-001, R-014, R-016, R-017, R-019, R-020, R-071 and R-098 cite TC-* files under .sdlc/slices/S-00x/verification/. The retention prune deleted those files, so later regression runs cannot re-run that evidence.

seeds.title: Wrong article in the missing-part Fail message
seeds.detail: The message reads 'a e2e-area branch name needs ...'. The spec does not define the message text.

title: tails: run, slice, milestone, e2e, e2e-area
riskReason: Wrong tails produce wrong names for the pushed run, slice, milestone and e2e families.

seeds.title: name output is not checked as a valid ref or a non-flag
seeds.detail: The new run, milestone and e2e rows build the tail from the given part with no shape check (ADR-20261009-045048 accepts this). A --id that holds '..', '~', ':', a space or a leading '-' gives a name that is not a valid ref. Under a plain '{name}' format, that name can also read as a git flag. No consumer calls name before S-008, and the loop passes only ledger ids, so the risk is low now. Fix: when consumers are wired, pass branch names to git after '--', or check the output of name with 'git check-ref-format --branch'.

seeds.title: The run_lower case in T-027 does not prove lowercasing
seeds.detail: The tail run-1 is already lowercase, so the case passes with or without {name:lower} support. Only e2e_lower proves it. Fix: remove run_lower, or do not count it as a lowercase check.
