seeds.detail: sdlc/S-001-attempt-x and sdlc/S-001-attempt- match the slice row of the table, so list --kind slice returns them with an odd id. This follows the table.

seeds.title: list_kind returns [] for an unknown kind through the API
seeds.detail: The CLI rejects an unknown kind with exit 2. The API returns an empty list, so a typo in a later caller looks like no branches.

seeds.title: argparse accepts abbreviated flags and a repeated --kind
seeds.detail: list --kin slice and list --rep <repo> succeed, and a repeated --kind uses the last value. Set allow_abbrev=False if exact flags are wanted.

seeds.title: list uses %(refname), not the spec's %(refname:short)
seeds.detail: The code strips refs/heads/ from the full ref name. The result is the same except where a tag shares a branch name. The plan allowed this.

seeds.title: testkit: no helper to create many refs in one repo
seeds.detail: The property test creates refs with git update-ref --stdin in its own file. A shared helper would speed other verifiers.

seeds.title: parse accepts non-ASCII digits in run and attempt tails
seeds.detail: Python \d matches Unicode digits, so sdlc/run-١ and sdlc/S-001-attempt-１２ parse as run n=1 and attempt n=12 and list next to sdlc/run-1. Two branches then claim one n, and name(run, n=1) does not return the listed branch. The spec writes the regex as \d+, so this follows the text and no requirement forbids it. Fix: use [0-9]+ or re.ASCII for the numeric parts in PARSE_ROWS.

title: evaluate applies one rule to a sample
riskReason: evaluate feeds the pre-flight verdict; a wrong True launches names a rule rejects.

seeds.title: Non-string pattern or odd regex raises instead of None
seeds.detail: Forge rules cross a trust boundary. A missing or non-string pattern raises TypeError. RecursionError or OverflowError from re.compile also escapes. Catch these in _raw_result and return None, or have S-012 catch them, to keep the never-block rule of R-035.

seeds.title: Regex backtracking can hang evaluate
seeds.detail: A pattern with catastrophic backtracking runs without limit. The plan accepts this risk because patterns come from the forge. Record it for S-012 to S-014.

seeds.title: Rule helpers sit in the name section
seeds.detail: Move evaluate and regex_error next to the rule code that S-012 and S-014 add, away from the name builders.

seeds.title: Pattern compiles twice
seeds.detail: regex_error and _raw_result each compile the pattern. Share one compile helper if it matters later.

seeds.title: Non-string pattern raises TypeError
seeds.detail: evaluate does not guard a rule whose pattern is not a string. Rules come from read_rules, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: T-R-072a overlaps T-R-033a and T-R-034a
seeds.detail: T-R-072a repeats the hit and miss checks of the four operators and the negate flip that T-R-033a and T-R-034a already pin. Its unique parts are the two bad patterns and the negate flip for regex. The spec names this test for R-072, so keeping it is acceptable. Optional fix: leave the bad-pattern cases here and drop the repeated operator cases.

seeds.title: No gap for exotic regex errors
seeds.detail: No test covers a pattern that raises RecursionError or OverflowError. The plan accepts this risk. No action needed.

seeds.title: evaluate raises on a rule with a missing or non-string pattern
seeds.detail: A starts_with rule with pattern None raises TypeError. A non-string sample also raises. The spec defines no such input, and the callers build rules. S-013 and S-014 should check that read_rules always gives string patterns.

seeds.title: evaluate raises OverflowError and RecursionError for some regex patterns
seeds.detail: x{99999999999999999999} raises OverflowError and 100000 nested groups raise RecursionError out of evaluate and regex_error on Python 3.14. The plan accepts this because only re.error is caught. S-012 and S-013 must catch them or the pre-flight crashes. A forge RE2 ruleset never holds such a pattern, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: evaluate raises on non-string pattern, sample or rule
seeds.detail: None or number patterns and samples raise TypeError or AttributeError. contains with a list sample returns True. The slice promises None for an unknown kind only. read_rules in S-014 must make rules with string patterns.

seeds.title: regex rules have no time limit
seeds.detail: The pattern (a+)+$ on 27 a characters then ! takes 4.8 s, and the time doubles per extra character. Branch samples are short and patterns come from the forge, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: One 120 s timeout in the first run of the hostile-input test did not reproduce
seeds.detail: Two later runs of the same payload finished in 40 ms. The cause is unknown and probably host load. No claim is made about it.

seeds.title: evaluate can hang on a nested-quantifier regex
seeds.detail: (a+)+$ on 40 'a' plus 'b' did not finish in 8 s. Plan accepts this; the spec states no limit. Hand to verify-limits.

seeds.title: evaluate raises on non-string input or a non-dict rule
seeds.detail: TypeError for non-string pattern or sample (38 of 40 calls), AttributeError for a non-dict rule, TypeError for regex without pattern. S-013 and S-014 callers must pass strings or wrap evaluate.

notes: Re-plan from scratch with the simplest approach; read failures.md. R-026 moved to S-014.

title: sample verdicts, bad patterns and check-ref-format
riskReason: A wrong aggregation passes a sample that a rule or check-ref-format rejects.

seeds.title: Sample '@' passes the ref check
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format --branch expands '@' and '@{-1}', so judge passes them. Run check-ref-format without --branch, or reject '@' and samples that start with '@{'. A later slice can do this.

seeds.title: Catastrophic regex can run long
seeds.detail: A pattern such as (a+)+$ can take seconds on a short sample. The spec accepts this. Send it to verify-limits.

seeds.title: Regex compile errors are caught in two places
seeds.detail: regex_error and _raw_result each compile the pattern and list the exceptions (re.error, OverflowError, RecursionError) by hand. Round 1 and round 2 each had to fix both places, which shows the cost. Add one helper, for example compile_pattern(pattern) that returns (compiled, reason), and call it from both. A later new exception type then changes one place. Non-blocking because behavior is correct and tested (T-R-035e to T-R-035g).

seeds.title: judge reason text depends on a second compile
seeds.detail: When evaluate returns None for a regex rule, judge calls regex_error to recompile and read the reason. If the helper in the previous finding returns the reason together with the result, judge needs no second compile and cannot print 'None' as the reason. Non-blocking.

seeds.title: A failing rule with no label passes the sample
seeds.detail: judge uses failed is None as the no-failure test. A failing rule whose label is None leaves failed as None, so the sample passes. A rule without a label gives pass. Use a separate flag for failure.

seeds.title: judge raises Fail for a sample that git cannot take
seeds.detail: A sample with a NUL character makes subprocess raise ValueError. ref_format_error turns it into Fail, so judge raises instead of returning fail. The spec does not say what to do.

seeds.title: judge: first failing rule without a label is overwritten by the next failing rule
seeds.detail: judge uses 'failed is None' to detect the first failure. A failing rule with no label stores None, so a later failing rule replaces it. A forge rule always has a label, so this is low risk.

seeds.title: judge and ref_format_error raise Fail or TypeError for NUL, lone surrogate and non-string samples
seeds.detail: NUL and lone surrogate raise Fail. None, int, list, dict, bool and float raise TypeError. Callers pass strings built from a validated format, so this is low risk. A NUL sample could give a fail verdict instead.

seeds.title: judge: a rule with a missing kind gets the note 'unknown kind None'
seeds.detail: The note is accurate but unhelpful. Low risk.

seeds.title: @{-1} and @ pass the ref check
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format --branch expands @{-1} inside a repo and accepts @. R-037 intends a refusal. Reject a sample that starts with @ or equals @.

seeds.title: catastrophic regex blocks judge
seeds.detail: (a+)+$ against a 28 character sample ran 9.9 seconds. The spec accepts this. Send to verify-limits.

seeds.title: judge raises TypeError for a non-string sample
seeds.detail: ref_format_error(None) and (5) raise TypeError. Samples are strings by contract.

seeds.title: regex_error and _raw_result catch exception types one by one
seeds.detail: The round 0 fix added RecursionError. re.compile also raises OverflowError for a repeat count above the C limit. One handler for the exceptions re.compile raises on bad input would close the class. MemoryError is not reproduced.

seeds.title: @{-1} and @ pass the ref check
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format --branch expands @{-1} inside a repo and accepts @. Reject a sample that is @ or starts with @{, or run git check-ref-format without --branch.

seeds.title: catastrophic regex blocks judge
seeds.detail: (a+)+$ against a 28 character sample ran 9.9 seconds in r0. The spec accepts this. Send to verify-limits.

seeds.title: non-string pattern or sample raises TypeError
seeds.detail: judge with a null pattern or a non-string sample raises TypeError. Samples are strings by contract, so this is outside the threat model.

seeds.title: @{-1} and @ pass the ref check
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format --branch expands @{-1} inside a repo and accepts @. Two seed tests fail. Reject a sample that is @ or starts with @{, or run git check-ref-format without --branch.

seeds.title: catastrophic regex blocks judge
seeds.detail: (a+)+$ against a 28 character sample ran 9.9 seconds in r0. The spec accepts this. Send to verify-limits.

seeds.title: non-string sample or pattern raises TypeError
seeds.detail: judge with a null pattern or a non-string sample raises TypeError. Rules come from the forge reader and samples are strings by contract, so this is outside the threat model.

title: read_rules reads GitHub branch name patterns
riskReason: The GitHub read decides the verdict from a live API; a wrong mapping hides an active rule.

seeds.title: Non-string pattern from the API can crash evaluate
seeds.detail: github_rule copies parameters.pattern without a type check. A rule with a valid operator and a missing or non-string pattern makes evaluate raise TypeError (re.compile(None) or startswith(None)). Fix: make github_rule set the kind to None when the pattern is not a string, so judge reports unevaluated.

seeds.title: Dot segments are not encoded in the API path
seeds.detail: urllib.parse.quote with safe empty leaves '.' and '..' unchanged. validate_format refuses such names, so this is not reachable now. Reject or encode dot-only samples in read_rules as a guard.

seeds.title: unchecked flag covers two cases
seeds.detail: unchecked is true both for a non-github forge and for a failed gh call. Only notes tell them apart. S-014 should keep the notes distinct when it adds the GitLab and no-forge branches.

seeds.title: No test for the gh timeout path
seeds.detail: read_rules catches subprocess.TimeoutExpired, but no committed test covers it. T-R-029a to c cover exit failure, bad JSON and a missing gh. Add a test with a stalled shim and a small timeout, or lower GH_TIMEOUT through a parameter. Non-blocking: the verifier ran stall cases.

seeds.title: ghShim duplicates the new stub-server testkit
seeds.detail: branches.test.mjs defines its own gh shim helper. The testkit stub-server.mjs added in the same slice does the same job (argv and cwd log, scripted output). Later slices (S-014, S-015) should use one of them. Consider moving branches.test.mjs to stubServer. Not blocking: the testkit is for verifiers and its own self-test passes.

seeds.title: Edge cases not pinned: non-dict list items and empty sample list
seeds.detail: github_rule returns None for non-dict items and read_rules with an empty samples list returns unchecked false with no call. No test pins either behavior. Add one small test for each if the behavior is wanted.

seeds.title: Slice rating is medium and fits the code
seeds.detail: The slice crosses a subprocess boundary, and the rating is medium, so the verification battery already applies. No change needed. The 119 tests in branches.test.mjs and the stub-server self-test pass. The diff has no comments in code or tests.

seeds.title: Empty parameters.name falls back to ruleset label
seeds.detail: The spec says label is parameters.name when present. The code treats an empty name as absent. The spec leaves this undefined.

seeds.title: gh timeout of 60 seconds per sample is a plan choice
seeds.detail: The spec states no limit. Many samples with a hung gh could take long in total.

seeds.title: read_rules takes samples; spec names read_rules(repo)
seeds.detail: Spec section 2 lists read_rules(repo). Code has read_rules(repo, samples) per ADR f2cc. Extra exports: make_rule, github_rule, RULE_KEYS, GH_TIMEOUT.

seeds.title: Rule union dedup is quadratic
seeds.detail: `rule not in result["rules"]` scans a list. 10000 rules take 1.24 s, 20000 take 4.87 s, 50000 rules took about 37 s in one call.

seeds.title: Duplicate sample names overwrite by_sample
seeds.detail: samples [dup, dup] make two gh calls; the second body replaces the first under one key.

seeds.title: Non-bool negate becomes true through bool()
seeds.detail: negate "false" and 1 give true. GitHub sends a bool, so the effect is small.

seeds.title: Failure note keeps all stderr text
seeds.detail: 200 KB of stderr with NUL and escape codes gives a note of 200045 characters, unchanged.

seeds.title: read_rules: dot-only samples are not encoded
seeds.detail: quote(safe='') keeps . and .. so the path ends in branches/.. . Git refuses these names and the spec fixes the encoding, so this does not block.

seeds.title: read_rules: rule fields keep the JSON types from gh
seeds.detail: pattern and kind of any JSON type pass into rules. judge raises TypeError on int, dict, list and null patterns. Keep only str kind and pattern, or make judge treat other types as unevaluated.

seeds.title: read_rules: failure note keeps raw stderr
seeds.detail: The note keeps ANSI escapes, CR and LF, and any length. A token in stderr reaches the note and any log. Collapse control characters and cap the length.

seeds.title: read_rules: quadratic rule dedupe
seeds.detail: 20000 distinct rules take 6 s because of list membership tests. Use a seen set of serialized rules.

title: read_rules reads the GitLab push rule and the no-forge case
riskReason: A misread push rule hides the one GitLab constraint and passes names it rejects.

seeds.title: Forge regex can run slowly on a hostile pattern
seeds.detail: The GitLab push rule regex runs through re.search against sample branch names. An admin of the forge sets the pattern, and the GitHub path has the same risk. Optional fix: bound the pattern length. Not blocking.

seeds.title: Nested tuples with a None sentinel in _collect_rules
seeds.detail: _collect_rules returns shapes such as (None, (None, error)) and read_rules must know that a None sample is a sentinel. Return (rules, error) per forge call and let read_rules build by_sample. This is a readability fix only.

seeds.title: Error handling split across two loops
seeds.detail: _collect_rules and read_rules both handle the error entries. One place in read_rules can serve github and gitlab.

seeds.title: GH_PROMPT_DISABLED is set for glab calls
seeds.detail: _run_forge_cli sets the gh variable for every forge CLI. It is harmless. Make it a per-tool environment if glab needs its own variable later.

seeds.title: Whitespace-only branch_name_regex becomes a rule
seeds.detail: A regex of only spaces gives a regex rule with that pattern. The spec only says an empty regex means no rule, so this is not a defect.

seeds.title: Spec wording: glab error means no rule
seeds.detail: Spec section 3 says an error means no rule, but R-031 says a failure gives a note. ADR f2c2 resolves it; the spec fix is in SPEC-PROPOSALS.

seeds.title: read_rules raises Fail for an invalid config.json
seeds.detail: With config.json '{ not json', read_rules raises Fail instead of returning the no-forge shape. It makes no forge call. The spec states no behavior. S-015 preflight must catch Fail.

seeds.title: Forge note carries stderr unbounded and multi-line
seeds.detail: A 200 KB multi-line glab stderr gives one note of 200037 chars with newlines, NUL and ESC kept. R-031 says <stderr>, so it follows the spec. gh behaves the same.

seeds.title: read_rules raises Fail on a config that is not valid JSON
seeds.detail: With an invalid config.json, read_rules raises Fail instead of returning unchecked true. The spec does not define this case. No forge CLI call is made.

seeds.title: A failure note is not one line and not bounded
seeds.detail: A multi-line stderr keeps its newlines in the note. A 100000 character stderr gives a 100025 character note. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: A whitespace-only branch_name_regex gives a rule
seeds.detail: The spec treats only an empty regex as no rule. A regex of spaces becomes a rule.

seeds.title: Public surface adds FORGE_TIMEOUT and gitlab_rule
seeds.detail: Both names are new and public. The plan lists them. Spec section 3 does not define them.

seeds.title: gh rule with missing parameters returns kind null and pattern null
seeds.detail: A gh entry {"type":"branch_name_pattern"} with no parameters gives a rule with kind null and pattern null, in the S-013 and S-014 code alike. R-026 acceptance says kind is one of four values and pattern is a string. GitHub always sends the parameters. Fix: drop the rule or give a note in github_rule.

seeds.title: A forge failure note keeps line breaks, NUL and any length of stderr
seeds.detail: Stderr 'a\nb' gives a two-line note. A 200000-character stderr gives a 200025-character note. The spec says only that the note holds <stderr>. Fix: collapse whitespace and cut to a fixed length in _run_forge_cli.

seeds.title: A regex of only spaces becomes a rule
seeds.detail: {"branch_name_regex":"   "} gives one regex rule with pattern '   '. The spec treats only an empty regex as no rule.

seeds.title: read_rules results share list and dict objects
seeds.detail: For a gitlab push rule, every by_sample entry is one list object, and its rule dict is the same object as the one in rules. A caller edit changes all of them. The spec states no immutability rule.

seeds.title: Failure note carries raw stderr: newlines, control characters, NUL and unbounded length
seeds.detail: glab stderr is copied into the note unchanged. A 2 MB stderr gives a 2 MB note. Multi-line stderr gives a note with newlines. ESC and NUL pass through. The spec states no bound, so no block.

seeds.title: Timeout kills only the direct glab process
seeds.detail: subprocess.run kills the child on timeout, not its children. A glab wrapper that forks a process leaves that process alive after FORGE_TIMEOUT. Start the child in its own process group and kill the group.

seeds.title: read_rules raises Fail when .sdlc/config.json is not valid JSON
seeds.detail: The plan notes expect a no-forge result for a config that is not valid JSON. The code raises Fail. This matches the loader convention, so it may be intended. No call to gh or glab happens.

seeds.title: A regex of only spaces becomes a rule
seeds.detail: gitlab_rule keeps any non-empty string. A spaces-only regex gives a rule that matches every name. R-030 says only an empty regex means no rule, so this follows the spec.

seeds.title: testkit: glab-stub cannot report leftover child processes
seeds.detail: The shim runs sleep as a child of sh. The test used ps with the stub path or the sleep text. A helper that reports leftover children would help.

title: preflight tests the mode's branch names and prints a verdict
riskReason: The verdict gates launch; a wrong ok pushes the rejection the spec exists to prevent, though the push reports it.

seeds.title: @{-1} passes the ref-format check
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format --branch expands @{-1} to the previous branch of the cwd, so a working branch named @{-1} gives pass. Reject names that hold '@{' before the git call.

seeds.title: Dead branch in verdict
seeds.detail: `if rules is not None and not rules: rules = []` changes nothing. Delete it.

seeds.title: preflight result built in two steps
seeds.detail: `cmd_preflight` builds the result with `_echo`, then `result.update(verdict(...))` overwrites the key `ok`. Build the output in one place so S-016 can reuse it with `fmt2`.

seeds.title: read_rules swallows a broken config
seeds.detail: `read_rules` now catches `Fail` from `_config_value` and treats the forge as empty. State this choice in an ADR, or read the forge through one shared helper.

seeds.title: Dead branch in verdict
seeds.detail: In branches.py verdict, the lines 'if rules is not None and not rules: rules = []' change nothing, because an empty list already stays an empty list. Delete them. This is a non-blocking style point.

seeds.title: Prose of tests.md
seeds.detail: Several lines in tests.md read as fragments, for example 'preflight prints no samples' for tests that assert samples exist. The lines say what the test lacked before the change, not what it checks now. Reword each line to state the checked behavior. This is a non-blocking STE point.

seeds.title: testkit: stub-server cannot answer by argv
seeds.detail: The shim answers by call order only. A per-sample GitHub test must script one step per sample in order. A change to the sample order would break such tests without a clear message.

seeds.title: R-040 duplicate name unreachable
seeds.detail: A working sample can equal a slice name only in mr mode, but mr mode has no other sample. The shared by_sample entry case cannot occur through the CLI.

seeds.title: --branch with an empty value is ignored in mr mode
seeds.detail: `--mode mr --branch ""` gives no working sample and exit 0, because `build_samples` tests the value for truth. No requirement states this. It is probably right, since an empty value cannot be a branch.

seeds.title: No real mode can give two samples with one name
seeds.detail: Duplicate names reach `verdict` only through a patched `build_samples`. The shared-entry design in the plan has no real path today. The verifier covered it with a white-box probe.

seeds.title: Preflight output carries command, args and given beyond the spec keys
seeds.detail: The plan keeps them for earlier tests. The spec lists eight keys. A strict consumer that compares key sets sees three extra keys.

seeds.title: A forge rule with a non-string pattern crashes preflight
seeds.detail: pattern null, a number, a list or a dict with starts_with, ends_with, contains or regex raises TypeError in _raw_result. Preflight exits 1 with a traceback and no JSON. Catch TypeError and return None so the sample is unevaluated. Test: preflight.verify-security.test.mjs:150 (A8).

seeds.title: ref_format_error uses --branch in the process cwd, so @{-n} gives a cwd-dependent verdict
seeds.detail: git check-ref-format --branch expands @{-1} against the cwd repo. In a repo with branch history, --branch=@{-1} gives unchecked and exit 0. In a plain directory it gives fail. refs/heads/@{-1} is invalid. Tests: :289 and :304 (A17, A18).

seeds.title: Dot-segment names reach gh as a path segment
seeds.detail: A working branch .. or . is not changed by quote(), so gh api is called with repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/.. . Skip the gh call for a sample that fails the local ref check. Test: :400 (A25).

seeds.title: verify-limits: forge regex with catastrophic backtracking hangs preflight
seeds.detail: ^(a+)+$ against a 41-character working branch does not finish in 8 s. re.search has no time limit. The spec states no limit. Test: :413 (A26).

seeds.title: Forge CLI stderr is copied into notes verbatim
seeds.detail: The rules unknown note holds the full stderr (300000 bytes held in A21). A token in stderr would reach the output. Truncate and redact. Test: :421 (A27).

seeds.title: github direct mode gives no rules-unknown note when gh is missing, gitlab does
seeds.detail: Direct mode has no samples. With gh absent preflight prints no note. With glab absent it prints one note. Test: :327 (A20).

seeds.title: testkit: attack-corpus has no ref-name family
seeds.detail: The corpus lacks git ref-name attacks (@{-1}, refs/heads/ prefix, trailing dot, .lock, bracket, backslash). A15 and A17 define their lists inline.

title: preflight derives a format from one simple rule
riskReason: A wrong derivation writes a format the rule still rejects, and the run launches with it.

seeds.title: Open round 1 notes remain
seeds.detail: branches.py is unchanged since round 1. Cap the built length in _shortest, quote the suggestion value with shlex.quote, and suppress parser warnings. Rule text comes from the repo admin, so the risk is low.

seeds.title: Regex parser import sits mid-file
seeds.detail: Move the try/except ImportError for re._parser to the import block at the top of branches.py.

seeds.title: labels built too early in _format_line
seeds.detail: Move the labels line below the regex branch, where it is first used.

seeds.title: Plan text differs from code
seeds.detail: plan.md says preflight does not call validate_format on the derived format. The code does. Update the plan.

seeds.title: Private re._parser dependency
seeds.detail: The regex literal builder uses private re._parser. Move it to its own module if S-017 grows it.

seeds.title: T-R-042i overlaps T-R-042e
seeds.detail: Both use the same a..b contains rule and assert the same suggestion. Merge the sample and rule assertions of T-R-042i into T-R-042e.

seeds.title: T-R-042h pins the call count of a faked verdict
seeds.detail: The test replaces mod.verdict and asserts the number of calls, which is an implementation detail. T-R-042g already pins the behavior. Keep the pr-mode case and drop the call count.

seeds.title: Regex literal fails for patterns with a case-sensitive tail
seeds.detail: The S-001 tail is the only tail tried. A pattern such as ^(feat|fix)/[a-z0-9-]+$ gets the text fallback, although the user could still rename the tail rule. The spec does not require more.

seeds.title: preflight crashes with a traceback on a non-string rule pattern
seeds.detail: A list, null, number or object pattern makes _raw_result raise TypeError (re.compile too for regex); preflight exits 1 with a traceback and no JSON. Code is S-015's, not in the S-016 diff. TC-cli-6.

seeds.title: preflight hangs on a catastrophic regex rule
seeds.detail: Nested-star regex (((...(a*)*...)*b on sdlc/state-<14 digits> does not finish in 10 s; preflight hit the 30 s timeout. The cause is re.search in S-015's _raw_result. See logs/cli-0-probes.txt.

seeds.title: rename suggestion puts the branch name unquoted into a shell line
seeds.detail: git branch -m <name> <new-name> uses the raw name. $(id) and backtick names run if pasted; quotes, spaces and backslashes read back wrong; a newline splits the suggestion into three lines.

seeds.title: _regex_literal builds an unbounded string for nested counted repeats
seeds.detail: ((a{1000}){1000}){1000} took 19 s and 5.9 GB peak RSS; ((a{1000}){1000}){100} took 1.9 s and 637 MB. A cap on the built length would remove the risk.

seeds.title: suggestion holds raw CR or LF from a rule pattern, rule label or branch name
seeds.detail: A pattern, label or --branch value with a line break is copied into the suggestion, so it splits into several lines. A forged second line can start with 'rename the branch'. The JSON stays valid. 26 runs are listed in cli-1-seeds.txt. The spec states no single-line rule for hostile input.

seeds.title: _regex_literal expands nested repeats without a size limit
seeds.detail: ^((a{1000}){1000}){1000}/x$ takes 14.7 s through preflight. ^((a{10000}){10000}){10000}/x$ made the process get killed (exit 137 after 71 s) in a direct probe. The pattern comes from a forge rule. The spec states no time or size limit for this slice. A cap on the built string length would close it.

seeds.title: _regex_literal builds a huge string for large repeat counts
seeds.detail: a{999999999} took 17.5 s and 5.7 GB; ((a{1000}){1000}){1000} took 18.6 s and 5.9 GB; (?:x{65535}){65535} did not finish in 40 s. Through the CLI, preflight took about 20 s on ^a{999999999}/. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: A derived format that validate_format refuses is reported as ok
seeds.detail: A starts_with, ends_with or contains rule with the pattern { or } or {x} gives ok true, derived true and a format such as {sdlc/{name}. validate_format refuses it, so the next run that reads it exits 2.

seeds.title: Rename line puts the branch name unquoted after git branch -m
seeds.detail: A name with a space, a leading dash or $(...) gives a command that breaks or runs differently when pasted.

seeds.title: A pattern with a newline splits the suggestion into two lines
seeds.detail: A newline in a starts_with pattern gives a two-line suggestion. A double quote in a regex pattern or label is not escaped.

seeds.title: A non-string pattern in a rule crashes preflight with a traceback
seeds.detail: A starts_with rule with a list pattern gives TypeError in _raw_result (S-015 code, not in the S-016 diff). derive itself refuses it.

seeds.title: An empty-prefix regex candidate is skipped
seeds.detail: For ^a*/S-1$ the only candidate is empty, so the text fallback appears although a/S-1 would pass the rule.

seeds.title: A bare --branch value that starts with a dash is refused by argparse
seeds.detail: --branch -x exits 2; --branch=-x works.

seeds.title: suggestion line embeds rule text unescaped
seeds.detail: A pattern or affix with a newline gives a multi-line suggestion that can start a second --branch-format line. A quote or $(id) in a derived affix or regex literal is printed raw inside double quotes, so a pasted line runs a command. The rule text comes from the repo admin, a trusted party. Quote the value and keep the suggestion to one line.

seeds.title: non-string rule pattern crashes preflight with a traceback
seeds.detail: A GitHub rule whose pattern is null, a list, a number or a dict raises TypeError in evaluate (startswith, endswith, contains). Exit is 1 with no JSON. The crash is in S-015 code. Treat a non-string pattern as an unevaluated rule with a note.

seeds.title: verify-limits: regex literal builder expands repeat counts in memory
seeds.detail: _shortest multiplies the inner string by the minimum repeat count. A 35 byte pattern such as ^(a{99999}){99999}$ uses 4 GB to 10 GB. ^a{999999999}$ takes 13 s. The spec states no limit. Cap the built length and return None above it.

seeds.title: FutureWarning on stderr for a regex with a nested set
seeds.detail: The pattern ^[[:alpha:]]+/ makes re._parser warn 'Possible nested set' on stderr. It is not a traceback. Suppress warnings around the parse.

seeds.title: Stale verification tests fail
seeds.detail: 50 old verify-cli and verify-security tests pin earlier source states (push guard pins) and already fail on the base. They are not part of npm test.

seeds.title: No test carries the exact spec title for R-073
seeds.detail: The spec Testing section lists the title 'derive follows the table and refuses regex, negate and several rules'. The deletion of T-R-073a removed the only test with that title. The behavior is covered by T-R-042b, T-R-042c and T-R-042f. A tracker that matches by title would miss it.

title: preflight edge cases and the forge shim suite
riskReason: The shim suite guards the unknown-rules paths; a wrong pass hides rules that will reject the push.

seeds.title: Non-string pattern guard is repeated in three places
seeds.detail: branches.py checks isinstance(pattern, str) in regex_error and _raw_result, and judge names the kinds again for the note. A small helper such as STRING_KINDS = ("starts_with", "ends_with", "contains", "regex") would hold the kind list in one place. Optional cleanup.

seeds.title: Seed: T-R-091a/b and T-R-074a scenario 4 overlap
seeds.detail: Scenario 4 in T-R-074a repeats the regex-pass case that T-R-091a pins. This is required by the spec's seven-scenario shim test, so keep it. No fix needed.

seeds.title: preflight is quadratic in the rule count
seeds.detail: The spec states no bound on the number of forge rules.

seeds.title: preflight is quadratic in the number of forge rules
seeds.detail: Round 0 measured 5000 rules at 1.5 s and 20000 rules at 18.9 s. The cause is the scan in read_rules. Real forges cap rules far below this. Not fixed.

seeds.title: derive treats an empty pattern as not derivable
seeds.detail: The spec table would give sdlc/{name} for starts_with with an empty pattern. derive returns None. The result is the same in practice, because an empty pattern passes every sample.

seeds.title: preflight output holds the extra keys args and command
seeds.detail: The spec output example shows no args or command keys. They come from the shared echo of the other commands.

seeds.title: the suggestion repeats rule text as shell syntax
seeds.detail: A starts_with pattern such as x" ; touch PWN # appears in the suggestion line as --branch-format text. Rule authors are repo admins, so the threat is low.

seeds.title: gh stderr goes whole into notes
seeds.detail: On a gh failure, stderr goes unbounded and unredacted into notes (200 KB and a token-like string reached the JSON output).

seeds.title: a rule pattern is echoed whole into the output
seeds.detail: A 20 MB contains pattern gives 41 MB of stdout. The spec states no limit.

seeds.title: the negate guard in derive is not needed for safety
seeds.detail: Removing the negate check from derive changes no result, because the second verdict rejects every derived format of a negated rule.

title: SKILL.md: the flag, the pre-flight bullet and the launch arg
riskReason: The driver prompt gates every launch; a wrong bullet ends runs early or skips the check.

seeds.title: User-supplied branch format reaches a shell command
seeds.detail: SKILL.md passes the --branch-format value to branches.py in double quotes. The driver must keep the quotes and must not use eval. Non-blocking reminder; no change required.

seeds.title: Mismatch bullet sits before the worktree is created
seeds.detail: The bullet 'After the worktree exists ...' is in Pre-flight, before the Launch step. The spec places it there, so the order is acceptable, but a driver that reads steps in order cannot apply it until the worktree exists. Add 'in Launch, once $WT exists' or move the bullet next to where $WT is created. Not blocking.

seeds.title: Rewritten stack-flag assertion matches across a wide span
seeds.detail: The assertion uses [\s\S]* between '**Branch format:**', 'first run only' and the resume wording. It can match text from other bullets. Use a bounded span, or reuse branchFormatBullet(). Not blocking.

seeds.title: Weak needles in T-R-046a
seeds.detail: The needles list holds the common words 'rule', 'notes', 'format' and 'samples'. Each word appears anywhere in the bullet, so these checks pass even when the clause that uses them is gone. Pin each word inside a phrase, as T-R-097 does, or drop the weak needles.

seeds.title: Weak match for the end clause in T-R-048
seeds.detail: The check `assert.match(mismatch, /end/)` also matches words such as 'append' or 'ending'. Pin the phrase 'report both and end' with one regex. The existing 'report both' check already covers most of it.

seeds.title: Prose-pinning tests are brittle to rewording
seeds.detail: All new tests match SKILL.md wording. This is the only way to check a driver prompt, and the plan accepts it. Later slices that reword the bullet must update these tests. No change is needed now.

seeds.title: branches.py non-string pattern hardening is outside the slice
seeds.detail: The diff adds isinstance checks in regex_error, _raw_result and judge. The spec does not require them and the slice plan does not list them.

seeds.title: cli: driver end-the-run paths have no run-time check
seeds.detail: SKILL.md is prose for the driver. The tests check its wording and the commands it names. They cannot run the decision to end on ok false or on a config.json mismatch. The ok false path with a forge rule needs a gh or glab stub.

seeds.title: preflight invalid-format verdict lacks samples, notes and suggestion
seeds.detail: branches.py preflight with a format that lacks one {name} prints {ok:false,error} and exits 2. The bullet tells the driver to print samples, notes and suggestion when ok is false. It has no instruction for the error key.

seeds.title: Branch format bullet adds a sentence to the spec text
seeds.detail: The bullet adds an On a resume sentence that R-046 quote lacks. It is consistent with R-097.

seeds.title: Launch text states the arg as shorthand
seeds.detail: R-049 quote shows branchFormat: "$FMT". The args object lists the bare name and a sentence gives the value. The shape stays valid.

title: SKILL.md names the run branch and checks the user's branch
riskReason: The rename check blocks a first run on a false match, or misses a collision and breaks resume.

seeds.title: The format mismatch check runs after the worktree is created, checked out and fast-forwarded
seeds.detail: The mismatch sentence sits at the end of the Run worktree bullet. On a relaunch with a changed format, the driver derives RUN_BRANCH from the new FMT, checks out and merges, and only then compares formats. The old bullet had the same order, so this is not a regression. Moving the sentence to the front of the bullet would stop the driver from touching the worktree before it ends. Optional.

seeds.title: Prose pins in prompts.test.mjs depend on exact wording
seeds.detail: The T-R-047 to T-R-121 tests use regexes with character-window gaps such as {0,300}. A harmless rewording of SKILL.md can break them. The tests pin intent, so this is acceptable. Prefer short anchors where possible.

seeds.title: The Run worktree bullet merges many separate steps
seeds.detail: One bullet now holds the gitignore check, the run-branch naming, the first-run and relaunch paths, the ff-only sync, the dirty check and the mismatch check. A split into sub-bullets would make it easier to read and to test. The slice does not worsen the structure, so this is optional.

seeds.title: Prose tests are brittle to wording
seeds.detail: T-R-121 and T-R-101b use regexes with fixed-width windows such as {0,300}. A harmless rewording of SKILL.md breaks them. Non-blocking: pin shorter phrases.

seeds.title: Slice rated low-risk but touches the launch driver
seeds.detail: The change to SKILL.md reorders pre-flight steps and moves the WT assignment ahead of the Git mode read. A mistake here would break every launch and resume. Run the verification battery on this slice.

seeds.title: branches.py parse: a letter suffix after the slice id parses as a slice
seeds.detail: parse sdlc/S-002x prints kind slice, id S-002x. The slice row accepts S-[A-Za-z0-9-]+ on purpose (split and fix ids), so a user branch like sdlc/S-002x triggers a rename ask. No spec text forbids it.

seeds.title: branches.py parse: Unicode digits count as run numbers
seeds.detail: parse sdlc/run-U+0663 prints kind run, because the pattern uses \d. list --kind run would count that branch, and n+1 could then name a different branch. A [0-9] class would close it.

seeds.title: branches.py parse: a trailing newline matches the $ anchor
seeds.detail: parse sdlc/S-002 plus newline prints kind slice. Git refuses such names, so no real branch triggers it. \Z would give an exact match.

seeds.title: parse accepts a trailing newline in the branch
seeds.detail: parse("feature/PROJ-1-{name}", "feature/PROJ-1-S-002\n") returns kind slice because Python $ matches before a final newline. Git cannot hold such a name, so the risk is low. Use fullmatch or \Z.

seeds.title: branches.py name accepts negative --n
seeds.detail: name --kind run --n -5000 prints sdlc/run--5000, which parse does not read back as a run. The driver computes n from the list count, so it cannot reach this.

seeds.title: parse treats non-ASCII digits and S-<anything> as loop kinds
seeds.detail: sdlc/run-٣ parses as run n=3 and sdlc/S-002x parses as slice. The spec names only sdlc/feature-x.

seeds.title: parse accepts a trailing newline
seeds.detail: The $ anchor matches before a final newline. Git refuses such branch names, so no real branch reaches it.

title: sdlc-loop.js names branches through the format
riskReason: The loop script names verifier branches; a mismatch with the module breaks verification plumbing.

seeds.title: T-R-051b duplicates the default case of T-R-075a
seeds.detail: T-R-051b still compares the default verify branch with branches.py. T-R-075a covers the same case. Keep only the source-literal check in T-R-051b.

seeds.title: branchName repeats the branches.py format rule
seeds.detail: The {name} and {name:lower} rule exists in JS and in Python. T-R-075a pins both, so drift fails a test. No change needed now.

seeds.title: T-R-116a repeats coverage of T-R-050a and T-R-050b
seeds.detail: T-R-116a only checks that branchName is a function and BRANCH_FORMAT is a string. T-R-050a and T-R-050b already call both and assert their values. Delete T-R-116a, or fold its typeof checks into T-R-050a. Not blocking: the test is cheap and its name is honest.

seeds.title: T-R-118 may overlap an existing parse test
seeds.detail: T-R-118 parses a slice branch under the plain prefix format. The parse test near line 947 already covers S-002 under several formats. Check whether that test pins the same kind and id. If so, delete T-R-118. Not blocking: this round could not confirm the overlap.

seeds.title: branchName passes the tail as a String.replace replacement string
seeds.detail: A tail with $&, $$, $', $` or a$&b is rewritten by String.replace. The spec text shows this exact code. Real tails hold ids, rounds, profile names and parts, so none holds a dollar sign. A function replacement or split/join would make it exact.

seeds.title: A format with both {name} and {name:lower} leaves {name} unreplaced
seeds.detail: branchName('AB') with a-{name}-{name:lower} gives a-{name}-ab. The spec does not define this format. Check that format validation rejects it.

seeds.title: Dollar-pattern tails are reachable only through a hostile slice id
seeds.detail: The tail comes from the slice id and a fixed profile list, so reach is low. Fix: pass a replacer function to String.replace, for example .replace(token, () => value).

seeds.title: Janitor test depends on shared real temp dir
seeds.detail: The scripts.test.mjs janitor test ages a dir in the real tmpdir. A concurrent janitor run by another agent can reap it and fail the test. Use an isolated TMPDIR for the test.

title: next-action.py recognizes branches through parse
riskReason: next-action drives every slice decision from branch state; a wrong parse resumes the wrong slice.

seeds.title: State-head fallback bypasses parse
seeds.detail: head_is in decide falls back to a startswith('state-') test through branches.split when parse returns None. R-054 says state heads must parse to state. The fallback accepts malformed heads (for example state-abc) and leaks branches internals into next-action.py. Delete the fallback, or move the tolerance into branches.py.

seeds.title: Thin head_kind wrapper
seeds.detail: head_kind only forwards to branches.parse with fmt. Call branches.parse(fmt, ...) directly, or use the wrapper everywhere (active_branch does not). Naming is inconsistent with the surrounding code.

seeds.title: Milestone head pattern narrowed without a test
seeds.detail: The old hold matched sdlc/M-[^/]+. parse now matches only M-<digits>. This is correct for ledger ids, but no test pins a non-numeric milestone head being ignored.

seeds.title: Spec-named test repeats earlier assertions
seeds.detail: The test named in R-076 repeats the active-branch, state/e2e merge and milestone-hold assertions of the first two custom-format tests. The spec fixes its name, so keep it. Optionally trim the earlier tests to the cases it lacks (lowercase, stale e2e hold, foreign branch).

seeds.title: Edited comments in next-action.py are long
seeds.detail: The slice reworded older comments, and some lines now run past 20 words. Shorten them in STE style.

seeds.title: merged_heads uses parse, not name()
seeds.detail: R-054 quotes a name(fmt, "slice", id=...) lookup. The code uses parse with ids=by_id. The result is the same for real heads and also accepts case-folded heads. The failures.md notes this deviation.

seeds.title: Non-string branchFormat crashes with a trace
seeds.detail: fmt comes from config with no validation. A non-string value makes branches.split raise Fail, and decide does not turn it into a StateError.

seeds.title: No test for the state head prefix fallback
seeds.detail: head_is accepts an unparsed head that holds the state- prefix and the suffix. No test pins this fallback.

seeds.title: active_branch compares ids without case in a case-sensitive format
seeds.detail: The compare lowercases both ids even when the format is not {name:lower}, so S-ABC and S-abc match.

seeds.title: spec-vs-code: merged_heads uses parse, not name
seeds.detail: R-054 quote says merged_heads is looked up with name(fmt, "slice", id=...). The code keys merged_heads by the parsed id instead. Behavior matches in every case run, so this is a wording difference only.

seeds.title: active_branch matches ledger ids without case under a non-lower format
seeds.detail: active_branch compares ids with .lower() even when the format does not lower-case names. The slice parse pattern is case-sensitive, so no case was found where it changes a decision.

seeds.title: Default-format decision differs from main for a milestone branch with an in-progress entry
seeds.detail: Main read sdlc/M-1 as a slice branch if its slices.json held an in-progress entry with id M-1. The new code reads slice kind only. State never writes such an entry, so the change is harmless and matches the intent.

seeds.title: branches.parse accepts a trailing newline in a head
seeds.detail: The slice, milestone and state patterns end with $, which matches before a final newline. A head of feature/proj-1-s-1 plus a newline resolves to S-1. Git and gh refuse such names, so it cannot occur. Use fullmatch.

seeds.title: Default-format stack hold changed for e2e-area and malformed milestone heads
seeds.detail: Under the default format in stack mode, main held the run on sdlc/M-2-e2e-ui and sdlc/M-1-. The branch ignores both because they do not parse to the milestone kind. This follows R-054 but changes the old behavior.

seeds.title: next-action.py does not run validate_format
seeds.detail: A format with whitespace, such as a b/{name}, passes through decide and matches heads. preflight rejects it earlier, so only a hand-edited config reaches this.

seeds.title: branches.parse: \d and $ accept Unicode digits and a trailing newline
seeds.detail: PARSE_ROWS use \d and $ without re.ASCII. A fork PR head like feature/PROJ-1-M-<fullwidth 2> holds the stack, and feature/PROJ-1-M-1-e2e<LF> gets a merge command. Fix: re.ASCII and \Z. Not a regression: the old check was looser.

seeds.title: lowercased format: IGNORECASE folds Kelvin sign into ASCII
seeds.detail: A local branch with U+212A matches ledger id S-K1 under {name:lower}. Creating it needs repo write, which is trusted.

seeds.title: state prefix fallback merges any ready head that starts with state-
seeds.detail: The spec requires the fallback. A green, mergeable fork PR head feature/PROJ-1-state-x gets gh pr merge in pr mode. Same exposure as sdlc/state- on main.

seeds.title: merged_heads uses parse, not name()
seeds.detail: R-054 quote names name(fmt, "slice", id=...) for merged_heads. The code resolves merged heads through parse with ids=by_id. Behavior is equal for heads that name() produces. Align the wording or the code.

title: state-write.py names and classifies branches through the module
riskReason: state-write creates slice and milestone branches; a wrong name puts a pull request on the wrong base.

seeds.title: format_of does not validate the branch format
seeds.detail: state-write.py format_of returns config.branchFormat without branches.validate_format. A format like feat~/{name} gives base-branch exit 0 with a name git refuses, and patch-slice moves HEAD before git fails. Call validate_format in format_of. Argument lists are used for git, so no injection path exists.

seeds.title: Branch created before slice existence check
seeds.detail: ensure_slice_branch creates and checks out the branch before patch_slice confirms the slice exists, leaving a stray branch and moved HEAD on exit 2. Same behavior on main. Check the slice first.

seeds.title: Non-string branchFormat silently falls back to default
seeds.detail: _config_value ignores non-string values, so a number, array or object makes state-write create sdlc/ branches while config claims another scheme. Refuse non-string values with a message.

seeds.title: Docstring still names sdlc/run-<n> and sdlc/M-1
seeds.detail: The docstring near state-write.py line 275 still says sdlc/run-<n> and sdlc/M-1. Reword it to speak of the run branch and the milestone branch, as the other docstrings now do. The round-0 review asked for this and it is still open.

seeds.title: Three wrappers repeat the same Fail conversion
seeds.detail: format_of, branch_name and branch_kind each convert branches.Fail to the local Fail. The pattern is consistent but triplicated. Fold the conversion into one helper later. S-023 moves the format derivation into main(), so fold it then.

seeds.title: fmt threads through six helpers as a loose argument
seeds.detail: fmt now passes through ensure_slice_branch, ensure_milestone_branch, prune_stale_milestone_branches, milestone_branches_with_open_slice_pr, slice_base and awaiting_merge_base. This fits the plan and keeps the helpers pure. When S-023 lands, consider reading fmt once from config inside these helpers instead of adding more arguments.

seeds.title: Prune now lists all of refs/heads/
seeds.detail: The prune loop lists every local branch and classifies each with branches.parse. This is correct for any custom format. It costs one parse per branch. The plan accepts this cost. No change needed.

seeds.title: patch-slice makes and checks out a branch for an unknown slice id
seeds.detail: ensure_slice_branch runs before the slice lookup, so an id absent from slices.json leaves feature/PROJ-1-<id> checked out before the refusal. The old code had the same order.

seeds.title: state-write does not validate a format for git safety
seeds.detail: Formats such as 'x~/{name}', '/{name}', 'has space/{name}' and '{x}/{name}' reach git. base-branch prints an invalid name with exit 0, and patch-slice returns the raw git error. branches.validate_format rejects these, but state-write does not call it.

seeds.title: non-string or empty branchFormat falls back to the default silently
seeds.detail: branchFormat 5 or a list gives sdlc/ names with no warning. This matches the spec's load_format semantics. No repo format file exists in this version.

seeds.title: prune treats non-ASCII digits and M-0 as milestone ids
seeds.detail: The parse pattern uses \d on str, so feature/PROJ-1-M-٣ is deleted as a shipped milestone branch. The old regex behaved the same.

seeds.title: base-branch prints git-invalid branch names
seeds.detail: With branchFormat feature/{name}.lock, or a format holding a space, .. or ~, base-branch exits 0 and prints a name git refuses. patch-slice then fails at git. state-write does not call branches.validate_format.

seeds.title: patch-slice leaves HEAD on the run branch when the milestone branch name is invalid
seeds.detail: advance_run_branch checks out the run branch before git checkout -b fails. Exit 2 and the JSON error are clean, but HEAD moves and origin/HEAD is set.

seeds.title: require_known_mode crashes on a config.json that holds a list
seeds.detail: AttributeError traceback with exit 1, from config.get. The code is not in the S-022 diff.

seeds.title: A non-string branchFormat falls back to the default without a message
seeds.detail: The plan note for VS-7 expected an error. The spec's load_format rule gives the default. The result matches the spec.

seeds.title: The branch_kind Fail path has no CLI test
seeds.detail: branch_name always raises first for a bad format, so the branch_kind conversion in the prune loop is not reachable from the CLI.

seeds.title: Branch kind accepts Unicode digits in M-<digits>
seeds.detail: branch_kind and the old regex both use Python \d, so sdlc/M-١ counts as a milestone branch. Behavior is unchanged from before the slice.

seeds.title: testkit: pycall cannot return a Python set
seeds.detail: pycall.py serializes a set with repr, so callPython on milestone_branches_with_open_slice_pr returns a string. The test wraps the call itself.

seeds.title: patch-slice leaves a branch behind for an unknown or hostile slice id
seeds.detail: ensure_slice_branch creates and checks out the slice branch before patch_slice checks that the slice exists. Exit 2 follows, with the new branch left and HEAD moved. S-404 does this on main too. Move the existence check before the branch creation.

seeds.title: format_of does not call validate_format
seeds.detail: A branchFormat such as feat~/{name} gives base-branch exit 0 with the name feat~/M-1. patch-slice exits 2 from git, but only after it moved HEAD to the run branch. Call branches.validate_format in format_of.

seeds.title: A non-string branchFormat falls back to sdlc/{name} without a message
seeds.detail: A number, array, object or true in config.branchFormat makes load_format return the default. state-write then creates sdlc/ branches while config names another scheme. Refuse non-string values.

title: state-write.py threads the format through its remaining paths
riskReason: The threaded format touches every state-write branch path, including the loop-economy matchers.

seeds.title: slice_side_branches has no caller
seeds.detail: The helper follows the accepted ADR and a source test guards the future commands. Keep it. Round 1 only added tests for prefix isolation and case rules; no architecture change.

seeds.title: for-each-ref loop repeated
seeds.detail: slice_side_branches repeats the loop of branches.list_kind. In a later slice, add an ids parameter to list_kind so one loop remains.

seeds.title: head_is fallback in next-action.py is likely dead code
seeds.detail: The state kind parses through branches.parse, so the prefix/suffix fallback in head_is only runs for unparseable heads. Remove it or document why a non-parsing state head must still match.

seeds.title: config.json read twice on patch-slice
seeds.detail: main() reads config.json and patch_slice reads it again. Pass config to patch_slice in a later slice.

seeds.title: Test spies on internals instead of behavior
seeds.detail: 'main derives the format once' and 'patch_slice takes fmt as an argument' replace `format_of` and `patch_slice` and assert the call count and the argument count (`args: 4`). They tie the tests to the internal signature. They are acceptable because the spec requires the refactor. The `base-branch` variant adds only a call count and a branch prefix. Prefer behavior assertions in later slices.

seeds.title: Source-text grep tests
seeds.detail: 'state-write.py holds no local regex for verify or attempt names' matches text in the source file (`-attempt-`, `-v\d`). Unrelated text can break it. It matches the spec guard R-083-b, so it is acceptable now.

seeds.title: base-branch accepts an invalid branchFormat when the answer never uses the format
seeds.detail: With branchFormat bad{x} and a slice with no awaiting-merge dependency, base-branch exits 0 and prints main. format_of does not validate the format. The behavior is the same before the change, and no requirement demands validation.

seeds.title: A config.json that is a JSON array gives a Python traceback
seeds.detail: require_known_mode calls config.get on a list, so patch-slice and base-branch exit 1 with an AttributeError and no JSON error. The output is the same before the change.

seeds.title: patch-slice with a format that git refuses fails late with a raw git message
seeds.detail: Formats such as 'has space/{name}', 'a//{name}' and '{name}.lock' pass format_of and fail inside git checkout -b. The failure is clean (exit 2, ok:false) but names git, not the format. Same as before the change.

seeds.title: lowercase format also matches upper-case tails
seeds.detail: branches.parse folds case for prefix, suffix and tail under {name:lower}, so feature/S-001-attempt-3 is a side branch of S-001 under feature/{name:lower}. The VS-4 plan note expected upper-case names not to match. The branch-format spec does not forbid it. A prune command built on this helper would also select an upper-case look-alike branch.

seeds.title: pre-existing tracebacks for a non-object or directory config.json
seeds.detail: patch-slice and base-branch print a Python traceback when config.json holds a JSON array or is a directory. The behavior is identical before the change, so it is not a regression.

seeds.title: slice_side_branches has no caller
seeds.detail: ship-prune and collect-verification do not exist, so R-083 holds as a helper plus a source test only. The ADR for S-023 accepts this.

title: janitor.py sweeps only verify branches through parse
riskReason: The janitor deletes local branches; a wrong parse deletes a run or attempt branch the loop still needs.

seeds.title: Format validation uses split() for its side effect
seeds.detail: main() calls branches.split(fmt) only to raise Fail on a bad format. Use branches.validate_format(fmt) so the intent is clear.

seeds.title: Attempt-id guard duplicates branch knowledge
seeds.detail: ATTEMPT_ID in janitor.py repeats the attempt shape that branches.py PARSE_ROWS owns. Move the check into branches.py when a later slice touches it.

seeds.title: Source-grep test pins implementation, not behavior
seeds.detail: The test 'the janitor has no V_BRANCH or V_ID' (skills/sdlc/test/scripts.test.mjs:1690) reads janitor.py text and rejects two names. It fails on a rename and passes on any wrong behavior. The behavior tests below it already pin the sweep rules. It is an acceptable red-first marker for R-060, but delete it later or keep it as a known exception.

seeds.title: Old comments remain in touched janitor code and tests
